FOREWORD

Standard ( First Revision `, was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 25 March 1985, after the draft finalized by Natural and Synthetic Perfumery Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council.

0.2 This standard was first published in 1965. The Sectional Committee felt that the standard should be revised responsible for its preparation with a view to bringing it in line with trade practices in perfumery technology and also to align the quality level of the material currently manufactured and sold in the country which is given here for guidance only. the gas chromatographic method which is being 0.3 In this revision, progressively used in the country has been included and the wet method of analysis for determination of ester content has been deleted. 0.4 Geranyl acetate ( C12H2002 ) is the acetate of primary ally1 alcohol, It is also known as 2-( tram )-3, 7-dimethyl-2, 6 octadienegeraniol. 1-yl-acetate. It is represented by the following structural formula:

GERANYL ACETATE ( Molecular Mass 156 28 ) 3

acetate is distributed widely in nature

and occurs in oils of to a smaller extent in oils of geranium, citronella ( Java and Formosa types ), petitgrain and others. However geranyl acetate palmarosa, neroli, produced commercially in India is obtained from geraniolex citronella Hence, oil which itself is a natural mixture of geraniol and citronellol. geranyl acetate available at present in India is mainly a mixture of geranyl acetate and citronellyl acetate.

0.6 The material is widely used in different perfumery compounds and mainly in conjunction with geraniol, the parent alcohol in rose compositions and for artificial oils of geranium and lavender. It is extensively used for compounding many kinds of perfumes for cosmetics, toiletries and soaps, and in the blending of artificial essential oils and Aavours. 0.7 In the preparation of this standard, derived from the following publications: EOA No. 11-1975 Standard for Association of USA, New York. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

GAS CHROMATOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS ACETATE A-O. GENERAL A-0.1 The chromatographic
conditions

OF GERANYL

given here are for guidance

only.

- A sample of the material is injected into the gas chromatograph where it is carried by the carrier gas from one end of the column to the other. During its movement the constituents of the sample undergo distribution at different rates and ultimately get separated from one another. The separated constituents emerge from the end of the column one after another and are detected by suitable means whose response is related to the amount of a specific component leaving the column. A-l. APPARATUS

A-O.2 Outline of the Method

IS:3241 A-2. A-2.1 PROCEDURE

- 1985

Conduct the flow of the carrier gas and inject the sample at inject port where it is vaporized and well mixed with the carrier gas. This is led into the chromatographic column wherein vaporized constituents of the sample are separated out by virtue of their differing As the different constituents pass interaction with the stationary phase. through the detector, they give signals corresponding to the amount of particular constituents leaving the column. The detector signal, on transmission to the recorder, plots the chart. From the specific area under various peaks corresponding to specific constituents, the quantities of different constituents are determined.
NOTE - For the separation tained at the temperature of the constituents. to be efficient, it is necessary that the column is mainsuggested throughout the time required for the resolution

A-3. A-3.1

CALCULATION

Area Measurement ( see Note 1 ) - Since normal peaks approximate a triangle the area is measured by multiplying the peak height times the width of half height. The normal peak base is not taken since large deviations may be observed due to tailing or adsorption. simple and fairly accurate when peaks are This technique is rapid, symmetrical and of reasonable width.
